`Core\Request::jsonAs`, `method`, `mount`, `scheme`, `path`, `query`, `queryAs` and `post`
owe nothing. Each has `about.md`, three examples, an attack, a bench and a Rust test that
carries `covers:`. The `query`, `queryAs` and `post` benches declare `calls 0` only: their
allocations (29 and 30 per read) count the parse of the whole parameter set, which the
module doc owns, so no allocation figure is declared.

`dossier-core-request-2-2` still fails on two members: `postAs` and `route`. Each owes
examples, an attack and a bench. Their Rust tests are marked, and their Novis cases
already exist (`postAs` through `// covers:` in
`tests/conformance/core/a-request-parameter-set-becomes-the-shape-it-was-asked-for.nvst`).

A parameter whose escape is not UTF-8 throws a `RuntimeError` naming the member the
program called (`Core\Request::query()`, `post()`), pinned by
`tests/conformance/core/a-request-parameter-that-is-not-utf-8-names-the-request-member.nvst`.

items.text: **`Core\Request::postAs`** — owes examples, hostile and perf (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). The member is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/request.rs:2311`; `docs/examples/core/Request/queryAs/` is the model to follow, over a urlencoded `--BODY--`.

**`Core\Request::route`** — owes examples, hostile and perf. The member is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/request.rs:1992`; an example needs a `#[Route]` the request matches, and `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/router.rs:2428` is its Rust test.

backlog: `nv proofs --run` reported an attack as unbounded after its timeout, and the `nvs.exe` it started kept running for over ten minutes on Windows. `killTree` is `tools/nv/lib/proc.ts:180`. Check with `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` after a timeout.

The `query` and `queryAs` attacks cannot reach the 256M memory limit within the timeout, because a 100-deep name makes each parse slow. The `queryAs` attack repeats a throwing read instead. The limit itself holds: under 16M the same keep-loop stops at once.
